set.approach: Leave the car at the lot by the Cape Chignecto Provincial Park visitor centre, then head along the shore westward in the direction of Refugee Cove, timing it for low tide. Arch Brook is the second major area along this coast after Mill Brook, and it can only be reached from the beach at or near low tide; outside that window you must rappel in. The route begins with a short rock step off the beach that leads to a broad ice flow, just right of The Crack of Noon.

review.notes: Route page: rock step then broad ice flow. Area pages: tide-gated beach access, rappel alternative. No descent stated.

set.approach: This stretch is remote. The best way in is by snowmobile, though skis, snowshoes or a kayak also work, and getting in and set up takes most of a day, so plan on camping. The route lies in an amphitheatre north of Big Bald Brook. Find the amphitheatre and drop in from either side, or, at low tide, rappel to the beach from a neighbouring line and walk along to the foot of the route. Pitch one is a steep curtain rising off the beach.

review.notes: Route page: location and the two ways into the amphitheatre. Area page: winter access and camping. No descent stated.

set.approach: This area is a long beach walk west of the parking area. The route is the third climb from the right when moving left through the area: a long, low-angle flow.

review.notes: Route page: third climb from the right. Area page: beach walk and tide timing. No descent stated.

set.approach: This area is a long beach walk west of the parking area. set.approach: Leave the car at the lot by the Cape Chignecto Provincial Park visitor centre, then head along the shore westward in the direction of Refugee Cove, timing it for low tide. The High and Wild area lies at the western end of this walk, and, as everywhere along this coast, it can only be reached on the beach at low tide. The first route in the area is impossible to miss, since it is the tallest line and ends in a big steep final pitch leading to the trees. It starts on easy rock, then an ice ramp, just left of Maritime Alpinism.

review.notes: Route page: just left of Maritime Alpinism, rock then ramp start. Area page: walk and tide. No descent stated.

set.approach: Leave the car at the lot by the Cape Chignecto Provincial Park visitor centre, then head along the shore westward in the direction of Refugee Cove, timing it for low tide. The High and Wild area lies at the western end of this walk, and, as everywhere along this coast, it can only be reached on the beach at low tide. Find it directly to the left of Living in the Spirit Of. Aim for the hanging curtain that the tides undercut, which never reaches the ground; gain its left-hand side by a mix of ice and rock, then continue to the easier snow and ice field above.

review.notes: Route page: start details. Area page: walk and tide. No descent stated.

set.approach: The usual base is one of the Big Bald or Little Bald Brook campsites, from which the approach is short. The area sits at kilometre 19 of the Cape Chignecto hiking trail, where the trail marker is easy to find. The climbs come into view well before the first spot from which you could rappel into the cove, and at low tide the shore is easy to move along. Chenoo is the first line met on entering the cove from the north. You can rappel in, or you can drop in near where the cove begins and walk the shore at low tide.
set.descent_text: The route can be rappelled easily.

review.notes: Route page: first line from the north; easily rappelled. Area page: camps, km marker, shore walking.
